hook.en: We cannot divide by a matrix, but sometimes we can multiply by its inverse, which does the same job. Just as 5 × 1/5 = 1, A × A⁻¹ = I.
hook.kn: ಮಾತೃಕೆಯಿಂದ ಭಾಗಿಸಲಾಗದು, ಆದರೆ ಕೆಲವೊಮ್ಮೆ ಅದರ ವಿಲೋಮದಿಂದ ಗುಣಿಸಬಹುದು. 5 × 1/5 = 1 ಆಗುವಂತೆ A × A⁻¹ = I.

objectives.en: Define the inverse of a square matrix

narration.en: We cannot divide by a matrix, but sometimes we can multiply by its inverse, which does the same job. Just as 5 × 1/5 = 1, A × A⁻¹ = I.
narration.kn: ಮಾತೃಕೆಯಿಂದ ಭಾಗಿಸಲಾಗದು, ಆದರೆ ಕೆಲವೊಮ್ಮೆ ಅದರ ವಿಲೋಮದಿಂದ ಗುಣಿಸಬಹುದು. 5 × 1/5 = 1 ಆಗುವಂತೆ A × A⁻¹ = I.

body.en: A square matrix $A$ is invertible if there is a matrix $B$ of the same order with $AB = BA = I$. Then $B = A^{-1}$, and it is unique. For invertible $A$ and $B$ of the same order, $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$. For a $2 \times 2$ matrix, $A^{-1}$ exists exactly when $ad - bc \ne 0$ (more in Determinants).
body.kn: AB = BA = I ಆಗುವಂತೆ B ಇದ್ದರೆ A ವಿಲೋಮೀಯ, B = A⁻¹. ವಿಲೋಮ ಏಕೈಕ. (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹.

points.en: Only square matrices can have inverses

narration.en: A square matrix is invertible if some matrix multiplies it, on either side, to give the identity. The inverse is unique, and the inverse of a product is the product of inverses in reverse order.
narration.kn: AB = BA = I ಆಗುವಂತೆ B ಇದ್ದರೆ A ವಿಲೋಮೀಯ, B = A⁻¹. ವಿಲೋಮ ಏಕೈಕ. (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹.
